notes: Inner Richmond (Clement / Geary / Anza, 19th Ave to 8th Ave), sheet 3 of the 1960 map. What the map shows here: thin lines (about 4 px) close each block and the street between is open paper; zoning borders are heavier lines (about 6-8 px) that either run down the middle of a street (x 1624-1632 and x 1738-1747 along the two sides of Park-Presidio Blvd; y 4502-4509 along Anza east of x 1747; Geary/Clement in places) or cut straight through blocks (y 3786-3794 and y 3930-3937 across the first row; x 1568-1576 and y 4170-4190 in block 1519-1619 x 4002-4228; the stair at x 1785-1805 y 4184-4310 through two blocks; y 4454-4459 and x 1447-1456 in the third row; y 4557-4566 and x 2028-2034 in the fourth row). Told apart by weight (a zoning border is about twice a block line) and by continuity (a block line always turns at the block's corner; a zoning border runs on across streets and blocks); the block's corner was put on the outer edge of its own thin line, also where a heavy border runs over it. The scan is effectively black and white. Judgment calls: (1) The two narrow outlined strips inside Park-Presidio Blvd (x 1639-1674 and x 1697-1736, every row) are typed as blocks because each has its own closed thin outline; they are the boulevard's landscaped medians, not lots, so the owner may prefer them as open. (2) TACOMA (a dead-end alley, x 1445-1497, y 4082-4086) runs into block 1403-1498 x 4003-4230 from its east side; the alley's paper is left as street, so that block's outline has a 5-px notch. (3) The small R-4 box near x 1752-1808, y 3935-4042 is drawn with heavy zoning lines over blocks 1752-1843 and 1754-1845; it splits no block. (4) The left column's blocks run past the box's left side in rows 1-2; in rows 3-4 their own left line sits on the box edge (x 1180-1183). Lettering (R-2, R-3, C-2, R-1-D, street names) is ignored.
